question: There are five clients, labeled Client 0 to Client 4, each requiring two operations to be performed in sequence. Each operation takes exactly 1 unit of time to complete. The operations for each client must follow a strict sequence: the second operation cannot start until the first operation is completed, with a minimum gap of 1 unit of time between them. Operations from different clients may need to be performed on the same machine, and no two operations can overlap on the same machine. To enforce this, binary decision variables determine the order of operations on shared machines. The goal is to minimize the total production time, known as the makespan, which is the time when the last operation across all clients is completed. The makespan must be at least as long as the completion time of every operation. Start times for all operations are continuous variables, and the binary variables ensure that operations on the same machine do not overlap. A large number (100,000) is used in the constraints to enforce the scheduling logic, ensuring that one operation finishes before another starts on the same machine. The problem involves determining the optimal start times for all operations and the sequence of operations on shared machines to minimize the total production time while satisfying all constraints.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "num_clients": 5,
    "num_operations": 2,
    "processing_time": 1,
    "min_gap": 1,
    "big_M": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n_clients = d["num_clients"]
    n_ops = d["num_operations"]
    p = d["processing_time"]
    gap = d["min_gap"]
    M = d["big_M"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.clients = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_clients - 1)
    model.operations = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_ops - 1)

    # All (client, op) pairs as a flat set for disjunctive constraints
    op_pairs = [(i, k) for i in range(n_clients) for k in range(n_ops)]
    model.op_pairs = pyo.Set(initialize=op_pairs, dimen=2)

    # Ordered pairs of distinct operations (for machine non-overlap)
    distinct_pairs = [
        ((i, k), (j, l))
        for (i, k) in op_pairs
        for (j, l) in op_pairs
        if (i, k) != (j, l)
    ]
    model.distinct_pairs = pyo.Set(initialize=distinct_pairs, dimen=4)

    # Variables
    model.start = pyo.Var(
        model.clients, model.operations,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=(0, None),
    )
    model.precede = pyo.Var(
        model.distinct_pairs,
        within=pyo.Binary,
    )
    model.makespan = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))

    # Objective: minimize makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.makespan, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence within a client: op1 starts at least processing_time + gap after op0
    def precedence_rule(m, i):
        return m.start[i, 1] >= m.start[i, 0] + p + gap

    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.clients, rule=precedence_rule)

    # Non-overlap on shared machine for each ordered distinct pair
    def nonoverlap_rule(m, i, k, j, l):
        return (
            m.start[j, l]
            >= m.start[i, k] + p - M * (1 - m.precede[i, k, j, l])
        )

    model.nonoverlap = pyo.Constraint(
        model.distinct_pairs, rule=nonoverlap_rule
    )

    # Makespan dominates every completion time
    def makespan_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.makespan >= m.start[i, k] + p

    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.op_pairs, rule=makespan_rule)

    return model

DATA = {
    # "five clients, labeled Client 0 to Client 4"
    "n_clients": 5,
    # "each requiring two operations to be performed in sequence"

    d = data or DATA
    n_clients = d["n_clients"]
    n_ops = d["n_ops"]
    p = d["proc_time"]
    gap = d["gap"]
    M = d["big_m"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.C = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_clients - 1)   # clients
    model.O = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_ops - 1)        # operation index within a client

    # All (client, op) pairs as a flat set of operations
    op_pairs = [(c, o) for c in range(n_clients) for o in range(n_ops)]
    model.OP = pyo.Set(initialize=op_pairs, dimen=2)

    # Ordered pairs of distinct operations (for disjunctive constraints)
    ordered_pairs = [(a, b) for a in op_pairs for b in op_pairs if a != b]
    model.PAIRS = pyo.Set(initialize=ordered_pairs, dimen=4)

    # Start times for each operation
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.OP, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Binary: y[a,b] = 1 means operation a precedes operation b on the machine
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.PAIRS, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence within each client: op1 starts at least p+gap after op0 starts
    def prec_rule(m, c):
        return m.s[c, 1] >= m.s[c, 0] + p + gap
    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.C, rule=prec_rule)

    # Makespan must be at least completion of every operation
    def makespan_rule(m, c, o):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[c, o] + p
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.OP, rule=makespan_rule)

    # Non-overlap (disjunctive) constraints for every ordered pair a != b
    def nonoverlap_rule(m, ca, oa, cb, ob):
        return m.s[cb, ob] >= m.s[ca, oa] + p - M * (1 - m.y[ca, oa, cb, ob])
    model.nonoverlap = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIRS, rule=nonoverlap_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "num_clients": 5,        # Clients 0..4
    "num_ops": 2,            # two operations per client
    "proc_time": 1,          # processing time of each operation
    "min_gap": 1,            # minimum gap between op1 end and op2 start
    "big_M": 100000,         # large number for disjunctive constraints
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nC = d["num_clients"]
    nO = d["num_ops"]
    p = d["proc_time"]
    gap = d["min_gap"]
    M = d["big_M"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.C = pyo.RangeSet(0, nC - 1)          # clients
    model.O = pyo.RangeSet(1, nO)              # operations (1,2)

    # All operations as (client, op) pairs for the disjunctive set
    ops = [(i, o) for i in range(nC) for o in range(1, nO + 1)]
    # Ordered distinct pairs (a precedes b candidate) a != b
    pairs = [(a, b) for a in ops for b in ops if a < b]

    model.OP = pyo.Set(initialize=ops, dimen=2)
    model.PAIR = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=4)

    # Variables
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.C, model.O, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # y[a,b]=1 means first pair element precedes second
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.PAIR, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence + minimum gap between op1 and op2 of each client
    # s[i,2] >= s[i,1] + p + gap   (op1 must finish, then gap, then op2)
    def prec_rule(m, i):
        return m.s[i, 2] >= m.s[i, 1] + p + gap
    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.C, rule=prec_rule)

    # Makespan dominates every completion time: Cmax >= s[i,o] + p
    def makespan_rule(m, i, o):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[i, o] + p
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.C, model.O, rule=makespan_rule)

    # Disjunctive (non-overlap) constraints for each ordered pair of operations.
    # Pair stored as (i,o, j,q). If y=1, (i,o) precedes (j,q); else reverse.
    # s[j,q] >= s[i,o] + p - M*(1 - y)
    def fwd_rule(m, i, o, j, q):
        return m.s[j, q] >= m.s[i, o] + p - M * (1 - m.y[i, o, j, q])
    model.nonoverlap_fwd = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIR, rule=fwd_rule)

    # s[i,o] >= s[j,q] + p - M*y
    def rev_rule(m, i, o, j, q):
        return m.s[i, o] >= m.s[j, q] + p - M * m.y[i, o, j, q]
    model.nonoverlap_rev = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIR, rule=rev_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "num_clients": 5,
    "num_ops": 2,
    "duration": 1,
    "gap": 1,
    "big_m": 100000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n_clients = d["num_clients"]
    n_ops = d["num_ops"]
    dur = d["duration"]
    gap = d["gap"]
    M = d["big_m"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_clients - 1)
    model.O = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_ops - 1)

    # ordered distinct operation pairs
    pairs = [(i, o, j, p)
             for i in range(n_clients) for o in range(n_ops)
             for j in range(n_clients) for p in range(n_ops)
             if (i, o) != (j, p)]
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=4)

    # Variables
    model.start = pyo.Var(model.I, model.O, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.makespan = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Precedence with gap within client
    def precedence_rule(m, i):
        return m.start[i, 1] >= m.start[i, 0] + dur + gap
    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=precedence_rule)

    # Non-overlap (disjunctive) - two big-M constraints per ordered pair
    def disj_first_rule(m, i, o, j, p):
        return m.start[i, o] + dur <= m.start[j, p] + M * (1 - m.y[i, o, j, p])
    model.disj_first = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=disj_first_rule)

    def disj_second_rule(m, i, o, j, p):
        return m.start[j, p] + dur <= m.start[i, o] + M * m.y[i, o, j, p]
    model.disj_second = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=disj_second_rule)

    # Makespan bound
    def makespan_rule(m, i, o):
        return m.makespan >= m.start[i, o] + dur
    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.O, rule=makespan_rule)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.makespan, sense=pyo.minimize)
    return model
